newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Latam stocks seen taking a breather.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen taking a breather.

text.p: Latin American stocks are expected to trade quietly at the start of the week, sapped by market holidays in the U.S. and U.K., but then build steam as the week continues, traders said.
"A little breather does no harm," said Inverlat broker Hector Jiminez commenting on the Mexican market but broadly echoing regional sentiment. Last week saw most bourses climb.

Among the region's five main stock markets, share prices in Mexico, Venezuela and Chile are expected to be firm, while Argentine stocks are expected to consolidate. Trading in Brazil is expected to be quiet because of Congressional holidays.
Argentine stocks are expected to dip on profit-taking after rising for 10 straight sessions. But bullish corporate performance promises future gains.
"The bolsa is attracting more institutional investors and is underpinned by strong long-term earnings forecasts for leading companies," said Zaracan trader Norman Trabucco.
The blue chip Merval .MERV index rose 3.4 percent last week to end at 767.67, up 6.2 percent so far in May.
"The market needs to consolidate but that doesn't mean it will drop ... it still looks strong," said one broker.
Mexican shares were expected to consolidate Monday after three straight record-breaking sessions, but rise again as several stocks that lagged last week's gains catch-up.
"After a downward adjustment we expect stocks to resume their short-term upward trend," said Inverlat's Hector Jiminez.
The blue chip IPC .MXX index ended up Friday 2.45 percent on the week at 3,988.29 points.
Brazilian equities are expected to trade quietly with Thursday a national holiday and Congress off until early June, leaving key constitutional amendment votes until next week.

Only Wednesday's auction of a 32.9 percent stake in Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig, scheduled for 0900 local/1200 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, is expected to hold market attention, traders said.
The Bovespa .BVSP index of the 48 most traded stocks rose 2.5 percent on the week closing Friday at 10,764 points.
Venezuelan blue-chips meanwhile continue to interest foreign investors as a package of labor reforms makes steady progress through Congress.
"There's a lot of foreign demand ... It looks as though the labor reforms are going well and that's viewed very positively abroad," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino.

The reform package, which passed muster in the lower chamber last week and is due in the Senate this week, is expected to liberalize labor markets and overhaul Venezuela's crumbling social security system.
Caracas's 19-share .IBC index closed Friday up 1.7 percent on the week at 6,746.69 points.
Chilean shares were expected to drift lower Monday on profit-taking after the market hit a three year high Friday after rains eased drought fears, helping hydro-electric stocks.

But last week's 4.5 percent gain, which took the blue-chip .IPSA index Friday up to 125.22 points, was seen extended later-on in the week on possible interest rate cuts, analysts said. On Friday the Central Bank reported lower-than-expected annualized growth of 3.4 percent in March and 3.9 percent in the first quarter.
((-- Caracas newsroom, 582 505 2600))
